section_overviews.commercial_observer:
Women’s Clothing Store Esti’s Takes 8K SF at 2263 Nostrand Avenue in Midwood: High-end women’s clothing store Esti’s is relocating to a new mixed-use development in Midwood, Brooklyn, Commercial Observer has learned. The longtime retailer’s 7,800-square-foot lease at 2263 Nostrand Avenue was signed on Tuesday.

Municipal Credit Union Signs 6K-SF Lease for New Branch at 162-15 Jamaica Avenue: Municipal Credit Union (MCU) has signed a lease to open a new retail branch in Jamaica, Queens, Commercial Observer has learned. The not-for-profit credit union, which has locations citywide and caters only to New York City residents, signed a 15-year, roughly 6,000-square-foot lease at Michael Rosilio ’s 162-15.

Hibachi Eatery Bijin Omakase Signs 5K-SF Lease in Long Island City: A hibachi restaurant is igniting the burner in Long Island City, Queens. Bijin Omakase signed a 15-year, 5,077-square-foot lease at the base of Trio , a nine-story, 34-unit residential development owned by ZD Jasper Realty at 27-19 Thomson Avenue near where the thoroughfare meets popular Jackson Avenue, according to.

Dongbei Chinese Restaurant & Bar Inks Deal at 63 Cooper Square: Dongbei Chinese Restaurant & Bar is opening its fourth location in New York City and its fifth overall, Commercial Observer has learned. The growing Northern Chinese dining concept signed a 2,000-square-foot lease at 63 Cooper Square , an East Village property owned by Matthew Rettner , according to landlord broker.
section_overviews.cre_daily:
San Francisco Centre Returns to Market at Deep Discount: San Francisco Centre is back for sale after closing earlier this year and losing a proposed redevelopment buyer in July. Brokers expect bids of no more than $130M, far below the mall’s $1.2B valuation from a decade ago.

Mall Values Jump 13% as Retail Recovery Accelerates: Green Street says mall values increased 13% over the past year, the strongest gain among 10 commercial property sectors. Limited new supply, resilient consumer spending and tenant upgrades have supported occupancy, rent growth and investor interest.

Florida Retail Leaders Put AI and Data at Center: AI and real-time data are becoming everyday tools for site selection, leasing, marketing, research, and operations. High construction costs and tight vacancy are increasing the focus on adaptive reuse, second-generation space, and flexible activation strategies.

Restaurant Traffic Falls 2.4% Across US in August: US dining visits fell 2.4% year over year in August, reversing gradual improvement recorded in June and July. Overall retail visits still rose 0.3%, but growth slowed sharply from 1.7% in July.

items.headline: Women’s Clothing Store Esti’s Takes 8K SF at 2263 Nostrand Avenue in Midwood
items.summary: High-end women’s clothing store Esti’s is relocating to a new mixed-use development in Midwood, Brooklyn, Commercial Observer has learned. The longtime retailer’s 7,800-square-foot lease at 2263 Nostrand Avenue was signed on Tuesday. Asking rent for the 10-year deal was $65 per square foot. The retail space at the corner of Nostrand Avenue and Avenue I occupies a large slice of the newly constructed property’s retail component, leaving just 2,700 square feet available.…

items.headline: Municipal Credit Union Signs 6K-SF Lease for New Branch at 162-15 Jamaica Avenue
items.summary: Municipal Credit Union (MCU) has signed a lease to open a new retail branch in Jamaica, Queens, Commercial Observer has learned. The not-for-profit credit union, which has locations citywide and caters only to New York City residents, signed a 15-year, roughly 6,000-square-foot lease at Michael Rosilio ’s 162-15 Jamaica Avenue , according to landlord broker Augenbaum Realty . Asking rent for the ground-floor space in Jamaica’s business district was more than $100 per square foot, according to the brokerage.…

items.headline: San Francisco Centre Returns to Market at Deep Discount
items.summary: San Francisco Centre is back for sale after closing earlier this year and losing a proposed redevelopment buyer in July. Brokers expect bids of no more than $130M, far below the mall’s $1.2B valuation from a decade ago. The WSJ reported the property is 93% vacant, with an ownership and ground-lease structure that has already derailed one deal. Key Takeaways The Wall Street Journal reports that San Francisco Centre is back on the market after closing earlier this year. A proposed buyer walked away in July.…

items.headline: Mall Values Jump 13% as Retail Recovery Accelerates
items.summary: Green Street says mall values increased 13% over the past year, the strongest gain among 10 commercial property sectors. Limited new supply, resilient consumer spending and tenant upgrades have supported occupancy, rent growth and investor interest. Major owners including URW and CBL are increasing exposure again, although mall values remain below their decade-ago peak. Key Takeaways The Wall Street Journal reports that malls have become the top-performing commercial real estate sector after years of distress.…

items.headline: Hibachi Eatery Bijin Omakase Signs 5K-SF Lease in Long Island City
items.summary: A hibachi restaurant is igniting the burner in Long Island City, Queens. Bijin Omakase signed a 15-year, 5,077-square-foot lease at the base of Trio , a nine-story, 34-unit residential development owned by ZD Jasper Realty at 27-19 Thomson Avenue near where the thoroughfare meets popular Jackson Avenue, according to landlord and tenant broker RTL . Asking rent for the space was $130 per square foot.…

items.headline: Florida Retail Leaders Put AI and Data at Center
items.summary: AI and real-time data are becoming everyday tools for site selection, leasing, marketing, research, and operations. High construction costs and tight vacancy are increasing the focus on adaptive reuse, second-generation space, and flexible activation strategies. Well-located Florida retail continues to attract capital, especially grocery-anchored, necessity-based, and service-oriented properties. Key Takeaways Florida retail real estate is leaning harder on data, AI, and physical experience.…

items.headline: Dongbei Chinese Restaurant & Bar Inks Deal at 63 Cooper Square
items.summary: Dongbei Chinese Restaurant & Bar is opening its fourth location in New York City and its fifth overall, Commercial Observer has learned. The growing Northern Chinese dining concept signed a 2,000-square-foot lease at 63 Cooper Square , an East Village property owned by Matthew Rettner , according to landlord broker Meridian Capital Group . Asking rent for the space was $21,600 per month, and the tenant signed a 15-year lease.…

items.headline: Restaurant Traffic Falls 2.4% Across US in August
items.summary: US dining visits fell 2.4% year over year in August, reversing gradual improvement recorded in June and July. Overall retail visits still rose 0.3%, but growth slowed sharply from 1.7% in July. September traffic will help show how much of August’s restaurant weakness came from calendar timing versus softer demand. Key Takeaways GlobeSt reports that US dining visits fell broadly in August while retail traffic remained slightly positive .…

items.headline: Lululemon Slows US Store Growth as New CEO Takes Helm
items.summary: Lululemon plans to open a net 35 new stores in 2026, down from its previous target of 40, while cutting 25 planned pop-ups. North American sales fell 12%, and global profit declined 1% to $1.5B, including roughly $135M in tariff refunds. The pullback signals a more cautious retail leasing environment as consumers reduce spending and brands reassess expansion commitments. Key Takeaways Bisnow reports that Lululemon is scaling back its US store expansion plans as weaker sales pressure the athleisure retailer.…

items.headline: Spirit Halloween Turns Retail Vacancies into Seasonal Wins
items.summary: Spirit Halloween opens roughly 1,500 temporary stores annually through a specialized leasing operation targeting vacant retail space. Flexible termination clauses let landlords collect temporary rent while preserving opportunities to sign permanent tenants. The strategy shows how pop-up retail can monetize downtime, especially when bankrupt chains leave usable big-box locations behind.…

items.headline: Shorenstein to Buy Fully Leased SoHo Office Property From Tishman Speyer
items.summary: Tishman Speyer is selling the 12-story, 155,000-square-foot office building at 148 Lafayette Street in SoHo, at the corner of Lafayette and Howard streets, to Shorenstein Properties for around $135 million. The Real Deal was first to report the sale . The deal was repped by Newmark ‘s Adam Spies , Doug Harmon, Adam Doneger , Marcella Fasulo, Avery Silverstein and Joshua King .…

items.headline: Nearwater Management Takes 38K SF at SL Green’s 245 Park Avenue
items.summary: Nearwater Management did not have to look far for a new office. The asset management firm is moving within SL Green Realty ’s portfolio from One Vanderbilt to 37,563 square feet on the entire 28th floor at 245 Park Avenue on an eight-year lease, according to the real estate investment trust (REIT). The two buildings are about four blocks apart.…

items.headline: Digital Financial Services Firm Zip Takes 13K SF at Rudin’s 41 Madison Avenue
items.summary: Zip , a digital banking company, is relocating to a new office space, Commercial Observer has learned. The firm, which specializes in credit and payment services, will move in April 2027 to Rudin ’s 41 Madison Avenue in NoMad, where it will occupy 13,394 square feet across the entire 18th floor, according to the landlord. It’s unclear where Zip is moving from.…

items.headline: Law Firm Greenberg Traurig Expands to 133K SF at One Vanderbilt
items.summary: Law firm Greenberg Traurig has no objections to its Midtown offices at One Vanderbilt — in fact, it’s taking even more space there. The law firm, which provides legal services to businesses, financial institutions and high-profile individuals, has signed a 10.5-year lease for 33,477 additional square feet on the entire 33rd floor of SL Green Realty ’s trophy high-rise at 1 Vanderbilt Avenue , according to the landlord. The lease brings Greenberg’s total office footprint at the skyscraper to 133,365 square feet.…

items.headline: IMG Worldwide Renews 90K SF at SL Green’s 304 Park Avenue South
items.summary: Global talent agency IMG Worldwide has renewed a 90,202-square-foot slice of its office lease at 304 Park Avenue South between East 22nd and East 23rd Streets in Midtown South. IMG arrived at SL Green Realty ’s 12-story office building in 2008, according to CoStar Group . Its last reported expansion in 2016 saw the company occupy seven stories there, with its footprint growing to 130,655 square feet inside the 210,000-square-foot building.…

items.headline: Harbor Fitness to Open 20K-SF Club at 3460 Nostrand Avenue in South Brooklyn
items.summary: Harbor Fitness has signed a lease for its eighth location in Brooklyn, Commercial Observer has learned. The Brooklyn-based fitness brand signed a 25-year, 20,000-square-foot lease at Gaama Partners ’ 3460 Nostrand Avenue , according to broker Augenbaum Realty . The space was divided evenly between the first floor and the lower level of the property in Sheepshead Bay, Brooklyn. Asking rent for the space was $40 per square foot, according to the brokerage.…

items.headline: Two Supermarkets Ink Deals Along Brooklyn’s Atlantic Avenue
items.summary: Two new supermarkets are coming to Atlantic Avenue in Prospect Heights, Brooklyn. The grocers will arrive at two of EMP Capital Group ’s newly developed residential projects two blocks apart at 880 Atlantic Avenue and 1042 Atlantic Avenue , Commercial Observer has learned. In the largest deal, CTown Supermarkets signed a 20-year lease for 8,400 square feet at the base of the 19-story, 237-unit 1042 Atlantic Avenue, also known as Prosper Brooklyn , which was completed this year.…

items.headline: Market Shifts, New York’s Uniqueness Mean Mamdani’s Grocery Plan Could Work
items.summary: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani wants to get the city into the subsidized grocery business. As his administration seeks a seasoned partner this fall to run its planned quintet of government-supported grocery stores, strong opposition means it won’t sail through the express checkout lane. Plus, a pair of new lawsuits could stop the scheme faster than you can cancel an Instacart order, and many critics decry the initiative as the first step in a descent into socialism.…

items.headline: Billion-Dollar Blockbusters Won’t Revive L.A.’s Film Industry
items.summary: Hollywood, or at least some aspect of it, had a summer. Between massive box office performances from “The Odyssey” (partially shot in Los Angeles), “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “Obsession,” the industry appears to have recaptured some of its cultural magnetism and moneymaking ways. Adjusted for inflation, the movie industry’s $4.76 billion summer ticket haul represented a 26 percent jump from the summer of 2025.…
